**RA Progress Statement — Winter 2027 Funding Review**  
**Reporting date: November 9, 2026**  
**Project: Seoul–Daegu honorific shift corpus (NSF-funded)**

The fall-term target was 6,000 annotated utterances. As of November 9, I have completed 4,200. I am the project’s only RA doing Korean annotation.

The current shortfall is tied to the approval timeline for the IRB amendment needed to add 14 new Daegu recordings. I sent the amendment to Prof. Hollander for signature on September 3. I followed up on September 12, September 24, and October 6; the emails are available. The amendment was signed on October 15. I could not work on the new recordings before approval.

While awaiting approval, I recoded 2,300 previously annotated utterances using the revised speech-level scheme requested in August. This work was not included in the original timeline and should be recognized as project progress. Since the amendment was signed, I have annotated approximately 1,900 utterances—more than 500 per week, compared with the planned pace of 350 per week.

At the November 6 lab meeting, Prof. Hollander described my annotation as “six weeks behind” and said she would note it for the review. That characterization does not convey the reason for the timing difference: the new recordings were unavailable for annotation until the amendment was signed. Without that context, “behind” may suggest that I was working slowly or carelessly, which does not reflect my work or pace.

At my current pace, I expect to reach the 6,000-utterance target by the end of January 2027. I ask that the funding review note include the September 3–October 15 signature timeline and recognize the recoding completed during that wait. If the note cannot include that context, I ask that the “six weeks behind” characterization not be included on its own.
